core.export: prepareRemovalFocus (new packages/core/src/removal-focus.ts, exported from index.ts with the type RemovalFocusOptions)
core.signature: prepareRemovalFocus(container: HTMLElement, control: HTMLElement, options: { item: string; control: string; fallback?: HTMLElement | null }): () => void
core.behaviour: Generalises toast-focus.ts, which stays as it is. Call at activation: returns a no-op unless `control` is or contains document.activeElement and `container` contains it. It records the item (control.closest of the elements matched by container.querySelectorAll(options.item)) and its neighbours, following items first, then preceding ones nearest first. Call the result once after the render that removes the control: it does nothing when the control is still connected and enabled, or when focus is on any element other than body, documentElement or a node inside the removed item. Otherwise it focuses, with preventScroll, the first neighbour still inside the container whose `item.querySelector(options.control)` is connected, not disabled, not aria-disabled and not inside [hidden] or [inert]; else `options.fallback` when it is connected; else nothing. Never throws and touches no global at import.

conventionConflicts.convention: angular-host-attributes (index 3): a kind-A host that writes role uses HwHostAttribute, never a host binding
conventionConflicts.conflict: HwHostAttribute writes the component's value while it has one. The alert always has one (derived from tone), so an application role on the host could never win.
conventionConflicts.closest: `role` stays an input and the host binding writes `role ?? (tone === 'danger' ? 'alert' : 'status')`. conventionConflicts.component: Alert dismiss, CookieConsent accept / reject, the last Chip
conventionConflicts.conflict: The rule needs a next or previous item or a container of the component. A dismissed alert and a closed consent region are themselves the container and are removed or hidden by the application; a single chip has no sibling and its parent belongs to the application.
conventionConflicts.closest: Chip hands focus to the neighbouring chip's remove button through core prepareRemovalFocus and does nothing when there is none. Alert and CookieConsent move no focus; their READMEs state that the application sends focus to the element the message concerned, the main heading, or the control that reopens the preferences.
